agree.reason: The plain apology and unchanged price will soften this household, but it is never told what happens the next time a storm thins the boxes, so its reason for leaving still stands.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the nets are correctly limited to tomatoes and peppers, though 'one storm is less likely to take as much of the season' is an inference the facts only partly support.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats raw facts and derives nothing: not the roughly $74 of produce each member lost (about $24.50 a week, half of it for six weeks), not what 52 shares left means for urgency, and not the survey result.

right_comparison.reason: It never sets up the household's real alternative, staying away or buying elsewhere, against what rejoining now offers.

qualification.reason: 'We can't stop hail' admits the risk but gives no checkable commitment, such as a credit for any week weather cuts a box by more than a third, so the reader cannot tell what they would get if it happens again.

objections.reason: The central objection, that the farm went quiet and gave nothing back when the boxes were thin, is answered only with an apology, and the pause credit covers the member's own absences rather than weather losses, with no promise of weekly updates.

fit.reason: It is a short email under 200 words, but it ends 'Thank you,' with no name or farm and gives no sign-up link or way to act.
